name: Banh khoai
summary: Banh khoai is a turmeric rice-flour crepe with shrimp, a quail egg, bean sprouts, and pork belly, folded with a salad and a thick peanut-and-pork-liver sauce. Vietnam Tourism places it along Kim Long. A stall price is check on arrival.
origin: Hue. Vietnam Tourism describes the crepe, the salad of fig, starfruit, and cucumber, and the peanut-and-pork-liver sauce.
howToEat: Eat it folded, with the salad and the sauce. The national page does not name a utensil.
Kim Long is the north-bank road where that page places the crepe, on the way toward Thien Mu. Shop names on the page are not picks here.
A clock hour is check on arrival. Treat it as a snack or a light meal.
where: Kim Long, the north-bank road toward Thien Mu. No shop door is published on this page. Check on arrival.
